entries.title: libvirt: Libvirt Daemons
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'libvirt daemons modular daemons virtqemud monolithic libvirtd sockets' on libvirt.org: result 'libvirt: Libvirt Daemons' at this URL; text: the monolithic daemon is libvirtd; modular daemons are named virt${DRIVER}d (virtqemud, virtnetworkd, virtnwfilterd); both are built by default. Companion result 'libvirt: virtqemud' (libvirt.org/manpages/virtqemud.html): sockets under /run/libvirt/ such as virtqemud-sock, socket-activated on systemd hosts.
entries.notes: Reference for the Day 1 task 'identify the libvirt failure mode'. A missing libvirtd socket is not proof that QEMU/KVM cannot work when virt-prefixed units are present.

entries.title: libvirt: Network XML format
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'libvirt network XML format isolated network forward mode none' on libvirt.org: result 'libvirt: Network XML format' at this URL; text: when no forward element is present the network is isolated from any other network; guests can talk to each other and to the host OS but cannot reach other machines on the LAN. No 'mode=none' value is documented. Companion result 'libvirt: Firewall and network filtering in libvirt' (libvirt.org/firewall.html).
entries.notes: An isolated libvirt network still lets guests reach the host and each other. The isolation acceptance tests of the plan (section 3.3) must therefore test guest-to-host paths as well; the XML alone is not a containment proof.

entries.evidence: Query 'path_resolution(7) Linux manual page permission checks search permission directory' restricted to man7.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL. The result text says that a lookup fails with EACCES when the process lacks search permission on a directory of the prefix, that the owner, group or other triplet is chosen from the process IDs, that Linux uses the fsuid, that CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH and CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE bypass checks, and that execute permission is granted by CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE only when at least one execute bit is set.
entries.version: Linux man-pages online copy as listed 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Authority for the Day 2 claim that a file mode is only the last element of an access decision: every directory of the path must grant search first. Use it for the toy-directory exercise and for the explanation of mode 0640.

entries.title: acl(5) - Linux manual page
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'acl(5) Linux manual page POSIX access control lists mask entry ACL_USER_OBJ' restricted to man7.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL. The result text says that an entry has a tag type, an optional qualifier and a permission set, that ACL_USER_OBJ is the owner entry, and that ACL_MASK caps ACL_USER, ACL_GROUP_OBJ and ACL_GROUP entries; the getfacl(1) result adds that the mask affects neither the owner nor the other entry.
entries.version: Linux man-pages online copy as listed 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Mechanism reference for ACLs on top of mode bits. The lesson must say that a plus sign after the mode string of ls -l means an ACL exists, and that the group bits of ls -l then show the mask, not the owning group's entry.

entries.title: bind(2) - Linux manual page
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'listen(2) Linux manual page mark socket as passive accept connections backlog' restricted to man7.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): bind(2) at this URL was the eighth result, next to the first result listen(2). Only the title and address were seen; the content of bind(2) was not in the result text.
entries.version: Linux man-pages online copy as listed 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Pair with w01-man7-listen for the question how a process creates a listening TCP socket. The claim that binding a port below 1024 needs CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE (or a lowered net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start) is not in the result text: write it ASSUMED or read it on the page before teaching it.

entries.title: listen(2) - Linux manual page
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'listen(2) Linux manual page mark socket as passive accept connections backlog' restricted to man7.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL. The result text says that listen() marks the socket as a passive socket used to accept incoming connection requests with accept(2), that the backlog limits the queue of pending connections, and that a backlog above net.core.somaxconn is silently reduced to it.
entries.version: Linux man-pages online copy as listed 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Kernel abstraction for the Day 3 and Friday question on listening sockets: a socket is a kernel object reached through a file descriptor; bind gives it an address, listen makes it passive, accept returns a new descriptor for each connection.

entries.title: ss(8) - Linux manual page
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'ss(8) Linux manual page socket statistics -l -t -n -p process using socket' restricted to man7.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL. The result text confirms -l (listening sockets, omitted by default), -n (no service-name resolution) and -p (show processes using sockets); the -t option was not in the result text.
entries.version: Linux man-pages online copy as listed 2026-11-18
entries.notes: Reference for reading a socket inventory. Which sockets the process column shows to an unprivileged user is not in the result text: the lesson must state it as the learner's observation on the guest (compare the output as an unprivileged account and with administrative rights), not as a quotation.

entries.title: systemd.exec
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'systemd.exec manual ProtectSystem NoNewPrivileges CapabilityBoundingSet' restricted to freedesktop.org, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL. The result text says that NoNewPrivileges= stops a service and its children from gaining privileges through execve (setuid bits, file capabilities), that ProtectSystem=strict makes the whole hierarchy read-only apart from /dev, /proc and /sys, that full also covers /etc, that CapabilityBoundingSet= removes every capability not listed, and that the effect of ProtectSystem= may be undone by privileged processes.
entries.notes: Directive reference for the service-hardening extension of the guided lab. The guest's own man page matches its installed systemd version and takes precedence. Read the passage on environment variables and secrets before teaching Environment= for a credential: ASSUMED: the page warns that unit environments are visible to unprivileged clients through systemctl show; the search result did not show it, so the lab has the learner observe it on the guest.

entries.title: Sudoers Manual
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'sudoers manual wildcards command line arguments fnmatch matches slashes spaces' restricted to sudo.ws, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this unversioned address. The result text says that wildcards in command-line arguments are matched with fnmatch, that a wildcard matches slashes and white space in arguments (unlike in the command path), that the arguments are matched as one concatenated string so a wildcard can match across word boundaries, and gives the example of an entry for /var/log/messages* that also permits an extra path argument.
entries.version: Sudoers Manual, unversioned address as listed 2026-11-18 (versioned copies from 1.7.10 to 1.9.16 also appeared)
entries.notes: Closes the gap noted in this file's gaps list (only versioned sudo.ws addresses had been seen). Authority for the question how an unauthorized sudo rule breaks a privilege boundary. The behaviour of the includedir directory (which file names are skipped) was not in the result text: state it as ASSUMED until the page is read, and test it on the guest with visudo -c and sudo -l.

entries.title: SSHd now uses socket-based activation (Ubuntu 22.10 and later) - Server - Ubuntu Discourse
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'Ubuntu OpenSSH ssh.socket socket activation ListenAddress Port sshd_config not applied' restricted to ubuntu.com, documentation.ubuntu.com and launchpad.net, authoring pass of week 1 (2026-11-18): first result at this URL, with Launchpad bug reports 1993869 and 2069041 next to it. The result text says that on Ubuntu sshd is started by ssh.socket, that this unit and not sshd_config controls the listening ports and addresses, that edits of Port or ListenAddress need a daemon-reload and a restart of ssh.socket, and that the behaviour varies by release.
entries.version: community post and bug reports as listed 2026-11-18; release-dependent
entries.notes: Community and bug-tracker material, not official documentation. Which release the lab guest runs decides whether it applies: the lesson says ASSUMED and has the learner read systemctl status of ssh.socket and ssh.service on the guest before editing any sshd listening setting.

plan_fact_checks.evidence: Search results on overthewire.org listed 'OverTheWire: Bandit' and the level pages bandit0, 1, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 20 and 21 (file banditN.html is the step from level N-1 to N). Pages 2, 3, 4, 7 and 14 were not in a result list. Game server bandit.labs.overthewire.org, port 2220; the site does not save passwords.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Section 16 item 9: the libvirt daemon guide describes modular virtqemud versus monolithic libvirtd, and an absent legacy socket is not proof that QEMU cannot work.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: libvirt.org/daemons.html ('libvirt: Libvirt Daemons') and libvirt.org/manpages/virtqemud.html in search results: monolithic libvirtd and modular virt${DRIVER}d daemons are both built by default; virtqemud listens on /run/libvirt/virtqemud-sock and is socket-activated by systemd. The RPM deployment guidance result says new installations should use the modular daemons.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Section 16 item 10: libvirt Network XML specifies isolated network semantics, and network XML is not proof of a complete containment boundary.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: libvirt.org/formatnetwork.html ('libvirt: Network XML format') in search results: a network without a forward element is isolated from other networks, yet guests can talk to each other and to the host OS. Guest-to-host reachability remains, which supports the plan's caution and must be covered by the isolation tests.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Section 5, Week 1 core sites: Ubuntu Server documentation is at https://documentation.ubuntu.com/server/.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: Search results showed 'Security - Ubuntu Server documentation' at documentation.ubuntu.com/server/how-to/security and 'Virtual Machine Manager - Ubuntu Server documentation' at documentation.ubuntu.com/server/how-to/virtualisation/virtual-machine-manager/index.html. The same pages also appear under ubuntu.com/server/docs/. The root address itself was not a result.
